name: lunastain

attributes.attribute: a cake baked at Lughnasa in the Scottish Highlands

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The lunastain is a cake of the Scottish highlands. It was baked for Lughnasa, the Celtic harvest feast held on August 1. A cake given to a man was called luinean, and one given to a woman luineag. These cakes were likely offerings or magical food. They guarded the eater and drew good fortune. A like cake called struan was made at the feast of Saint Michael.

okr.objective: Describe the lunastain cake of the Scottish Highlands.
key_results: Name the lunastain as a cake baked in the Scottish Highlands
Bake it for Lughnasa, the harvest feast on the first of August
